proposals.evidence: DEDR 3684 records singular Tamil nī, Kannada nīnu, Kodagu nīnï, Gondi immā/nimma, Kui īnu, Kurux/Malto nīn and Tulu ī. Only singular paradigm members are selected; plural nīm/nīvu and overt plurals are excluded even where the prompt simply says you. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: Propose ordered ten + six. DEDR3918 documents the patiṉ-/padn-/pon- combining forms of ten in these teens, and DEDR2485 gives āṟu/ār six and explicitly Toda pāṟ sixteen. The southern census variants retain contraction, p/h alternation and vowel notation; uncertain census lect labels remain source qualifications, not corrections.

proposals.evidence: Propose ordered four × ten. DEDR3655 and3918 explicitly give Tamil nāṟpatu/nāppatu, Malayalam nālpatu, Kannada nālvattu and Kota nālvat forty. Survey forms are comparative variants of these formations, preserving assimilation, reduced vowels and final vowels. No independent one-stem etymology is substituted for the two numeral components.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5159 gives Tamil/Malayalam āṟu river with Tamil oblique āṟṟu-. These survey ārɨ/āru/āttɨ river responses are comparative simple-stem correspondences, retaining the rhotic/geminate and final-vowel transcriptions. Minority lects absent from the article are not presented as literal attestations; inheritance versus local transmission remains reviewable. Longer river-bank and large-river responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
